clue.text: He probably knows a South American footballer, missing centre-back, white clothes

indicators.note: clothes means the pale word wraps round the turned name, dressing it

parts.note: wan means pale, white-faced

indicators.note: back means the shortened name is read from the end to the start
missing the centre means the middle letter of the footballer's name drops out

parts.note: Lionel Messi, the Argentine striker

explanation.surface: A knowing fan identifies a South American player who is out of the side, sporting a white kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-back' looks like a defender's position but splits into two signals: 'missing centre' drops the middle S of the name, and 'back' then turns what is left round.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise man is a sage, someone who in all probability knows the answers.

clue.text: Musical put on stage to nurture traditional character

indicators.note: put on signals that the next pieces are attached after the musical's name

parts.note: Wicked is the stage musical about the witches of Oz
a step is a stage in a process
to mother is to nurture and care for

explanation.surface: A musical is staged in order to foster a classic role.
explanation.walkthrough: The wicked stepmother is a stock villain of fairy tales and British pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The cruel second wife is a stock villain of fairy tales such as Cinderella, so a traditional story figure.

clue.text: It lines identical old fabric

indicators.note: lines means the word for identical has the other piece placed inside it, as a lining

parts.note: identical means the same

explanation.surface: Something lines a garment with the same antique cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Samite is a heavy silk cloth, often woven with gold, worn in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Pole has introduced island to Aussie's food

indicators.note: has introduced means the pole word takes the island and 'to' into its middle

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole
Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor has brought island produce to an Australian's table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin crisp toast is named after the Australian soprano Dame Nellie Melba, so it is an Aussie's food.

clue.text: Chip in minimum of oil, hot vessel lifted

indicators.note: lifted means the vessel word is turned upward, reading bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: a can is a vessel
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, its first letter

explanation.surface: A chip is dropped into a hot pan with a little oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, served with melted cheese and toppings.

clue.text: British fighter once offered inducement using Arab carrier

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or bribe
with means using, as in 'cut with a knife'
the camel carries goods and people in the Arab world

explanation.surface: A British soldier was once bribed into riding a camel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sopwith Camel was a British biplane of the First World War, a fighter aircraft.

clue.text: Disoriented one day in jet

indicators.note: in means the card and calendar letters sit inside the word for a jet

parts.note: a spout is a jet of liquid
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A traveller feels lost after a day on a jet plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' looks like an aircraft but is a spout of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spaced out is slang for being dazed and confused, unable to get your bearings.

clue.text: Immediate sensation of a breaking leg?

definitions.text: Immediate sensation of a breaking leg?

indicators.note: breaking means the letter goes into the leg word, splitting it

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so a leg is a pin

explanation.surface: What you first feel when you fracture a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: A breaks into PIN, and pain is what a broken leg first brings.
explanation.definitionFit: The first thing felt from a fracture is hurt, physical suffering.

clue.text: One taking someone off duty list tiny boy and I set up

indicators.note: set up means all three pieces are put upside down, read upward in this down entry

parts.note: a rota is a list of who is on duty
Tiny Tim is the sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: Someone takes a person off the duty roster, which a small lad and I have arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking someone off' means mimicking, not removing from the rota.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, so a mimic or impersonator does it.

clue.text: Castle contracted to host bash after good day for old emperor

indicators.note: after means the shortened piece and its guest follow the greeting

parts.note: hi is a greeting, like good day

indicators.note: to host means the shortened chess piece takes the blow word inside it
contracted means the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: the castle in chess is also called a rook
to hit is to bash

explanation.surface: A castle is shrunk to hold a party after a good day for an emperor of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a party but is a blow. ROOK loses its K to give ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirohito was Japan's emperor from 1926 to 1989, reigning through the Second World War.

clue.text: See 5
What might explain use of air rifle on leader in conflict

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter
use of the gun's letters means putting them to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Firing an air rifle at the head of a war needs some justification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use of' reworks AIR RIFLE into LARIFIER, which follows C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes matters clear can explain them, an elucidator.

clue.text: Position where very old revolutionary caught by old bullet

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: caught by means the turned letters are held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a tracer is a bullet that leaves a visible trail

indicators.note: revolutionary means the two letters turn round

explanation.surface: An elderly rebel was shot by an antique bullet.
explanation.walkthrough: VO turned gives OV, held inside EXTRACER. Extra cover is a fielding position in cricket, between cover and mid-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra cover is a fielding place in cricket on the off side, so a fielder's position.

clue.text: Thus detailed humorous way to (refreshingly) stop swearing!

definitions.text: Thus detailed humorous way to (refreshingly) stop swearing!

indicators.note: refreshingly means the letters are freshly rearranged, made new
detailed means the first word loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jokey way to cure a potty mouth: rinse it out.
explanation.walkthrough: THU (Thus with its tail cut) plus HUMOROUS and WAY TO is reworked by '(refreshingly)'. The phrase is what a parent says to a child who swears, once with soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The scolding phrase tells a swearer to clean up their language, half-jokingly suggesting soap as a cure.

clue.text: See 1
See 12
Offensive uprising

definitions.meaning: an uprising is people rising in rebellion, rising up

explanation.definitionFit: Disgusting is one sense; rising up in rebellion against authority is the other.

clue.text: Shortage of baby food in part of the UK, those beastly things blubbered?

indicators.note: in means the shortened biscuit is placed inside the name of the nation

parts.note: Wales is one of the four nations of the UK

indicators.note: shortage means the biscuit word comes up short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a rusk is a hard biscuit given to teething babies

explanation.surface: A lack of baby food in Wales leaves those wretched things crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubbered' looks like 'cried' but means covered in blubber. RUSK loses its K to give RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The big tusked sea mammals carry thick blubber, so the beasts are blubbered.

clue.text: Collected by wife half cut, hear me performing Show Me The Way To Go Home?

definitions.text: Show Me The Way To Go Home?

indicators.note: collected by means the reworked letters are gathered inside the halved word
half cut means only the first half of the word stays
performing means the letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tipsy husband, picked up by his wife, sings the old drinking song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' also means drunk, which suits the song; here it keeps only the first half of 'wife'.
explanation.definitionFit: The drunkard's question asks for directions, just as the song's title begs to be guided home.

clue.text: Heads rolling, I check copy in binder

indicators.note: rolling heads are tumbling, so the word's letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: to vet is to check
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: As heads roll, I scrutinise a duplicate in a ring binder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky tape binds things together, so it is a binder.

clue.text: Wipe bum

definitions.meaning: to wipe is to clean with a soft wet cloth
to bum is to cadge, scrounge off others

explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning with a soft cloth is one sense; scrounging off people is the other, as a verb.

clue.text: Line up that there drawer

indicators.note: up means the line word is read upward in this down entry

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
yon is an old or dialect word for that over there

explanation.surface: Arrange that chest of drawers over there in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture but is something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax colouring stick is used for drawing, so it is a drawer.

clue.text: Red choice

definitions.meaning: red here means meat cooked lightly, still pink-red inside
choice means fine, excellent, unusually good

explanation.definitionFit: Underdone steak is one sense; uncommonly fine quality is the other.

clue.text: Boot finding flea, say, on some ground

indicators.note: on means the jumper follows the lump of earth

parts.note: a clod is a lump of earth
a flea is an example of a hopper, something that jumps

explanation.surface: Someone checks their boot and finds a flea on the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a large heavy shoe or boot.

clue.text: Jerk knocking insect on hollow wood over

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned over, read upward in this down entry

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: hollow means the word is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A jerk knocks an insect off hollow timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like a jolt but is a fool. BEE above WD, read upward, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a boring, socially inept person, a nerd, as is a jerk in slang.

clue.text: Female animal, the Queen's dog?

indicators.note: the Queen's way of saying it means the cut-glass royal accent, in which the vowel of the dog word flattens

parts.note: a hound is a hunting dog

explanation.surface: A female beast, the monarch's pet dog?
explanation.walkthrough: Plummy royal speech, as mocked in Steve Bell's Guardian cartoons, turns 'hound' into 'hind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hind is a female deer, especially of the red deer.

clue.text: Support pronouncement of Scilly Isles a bit?

indicators.note: the sound of the islands' name is 'silly', and silly letters are jumbled ones

explanation.surface: A question of whether the Scilly Isles, off Cornwall, could be propped up a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isles of Scilly lie off Cornwall's tip; their name sounds like 'silly', which tells you to rearrange ISLES A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To support something is to steady it, to make it firm.

clue.text: Picked up, like a Tiller girl who's attractive?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, said aloud

parts.note: 'a Tiller' sounds like Attila, king of the Huns, so like him is Hun-like, said as hunny

explanation.surface: A leggy Tiller Girl dancer catches everyone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tiller Girls were a famous British high-kicking dance troupe; split, 'a Tiller' sounds like Attila the Hun.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive young woman is called a honey, a sweet one.

clue.text: Party sealing lips, minding language

indicators.note: minding means looking after, so the edge letters hold the language inside
the lips of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: Hindi is a language of India

explanation.surface: A get-together where everyone keeps their mouth shut and watches their words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealing lips' looks like keeping quiet; it is the outer letters S and G of 'sealing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively party or noisy celebration.

clue.text: Stick olive finally in drink, don't wait!

parts.note: a bar is a stick, as of chocolate or metal

indicators.note: in means the final letter of the fruit goes inside the spirit

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pop an olive into a gin and drink it at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in is to burst in rudely rather than wait to be admitted.
